Content: In `text(February 1938)`, a Works Progress Administration writer interviewed Roland Damiani, an Italian immigrant. Read the excerpt from the interview.

:box:My fellow Italians have elected me to many positions, because they appreciate learning and wish themselves to become true Americans. You are right. The children of Italian immigrants wish most of all to become Americans. They make haste to adopt the American customs and speech. In fact they worry and grieve their parents, who cannot understand or keep pace with them. It is not a little tragic sometimes — this conflict between the children and their elders.

	—Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, WPA Federal Writers’ Project Collection
Which action `ultext(most)` likely contributed to the assimilation of immigrant children into American culture?

A.Choice: attending public schools

Key.Rationale: Attending public schools most likely contributed to the assimilation of immigrant children into American culture.

C.Choice: living in ethnic neighborhoods

D.Choice: working in family-owned businesses

:box:In `1620`, the Pilgrims arrived in America to form a new colony. They wanted to live where they could worship as they wished. Before landing at Plymouth, the Pilgrims created the Mayflower Compact, a document that established self-government. They agreed to make laws that would be fair and for the general good of all. Content: Match `text(each feature)` to the type of community where it is most often found.

William Clark and Meriwether Lewis led an expedition for President Thomas Jefferson after the United States purchased land west of the Mississippi River. Lewis and Clark did not travel alone, however. They needed help from people who knew the land and the people they would encounter. `text(Two)` people, in particular, were very important to the success of the expedition. York, an enslaved man, and Sacagawea, a Shoshone woman, were part of the expedition. Jefferson wanted to know more about the West. The information in the box is an adapted version of a journal entry written by William Clark in `1804`.

:box:The prairies come within a short distance of the river on `text(each side)`. The prairies contain plums, raspberries, large amounts of wild apples, and a number of deer. We camped on an island situated on the south side of the river opposite some larger than normal hills. The hills were about `160` or `text(180 feet)` high.

	—William Clark, `text(Monday, June 25, 1804)`
Why did William Clark `ultext(most)` likely write this journal entry?

A.Choice: to describe available food and water sources on the plains

Key.Rationale: The journal entry describes the land in the territory explored by Lewis and Clark.

B.Choice: to report the living conditions of the native people in the region

C.Choice: to discourage settlement because of the high mountains to cross

D.Choice: to show that more expeditions should be funded to explore the area

:box:`ultext(A Mayor’s Race in Oakton)`

`1`. Maya Jackson decides to run for mayor of Oakton.
`2`. Maya hires Justin Yang to run her campaign.
`3`. Newspaper reporter Katie Parker writes articles about Jackson’s campaign.
`4`. Michael Booker registers to vote in the election.
`5`. Tyler Williams knocks on doors in his neighborhood, asking people to vote for Maya.
`6`. Ashley Cruz helps people vote at the polling place on Election Day.
How are Tyler and Ashley `ultext(most)` alike?

A.Choice: They register new voters in the city.

B.Choice: They propose new laws for the city.

C.Choice: They volunteer to help in an election.

Key.Rationale: Tyler and Ashley both volunteer to help in an election.

D.Choice: They organize events for a campaign.

Content: Match the name of `text(each technology)` to the description of how this technology has changed the way people live.

In the `text(early 1900s)`, some factory owners hired children as workers. Many Americans did not like this idea. The U.S. government wrote a bill to control child labor. Before the bill became law, people wrote letters describing their viewpoints on this issue. Read the excerpts of `text(two)` of these letters.

:box:Sir, I was haunted for `text(days)` . . . when I `text(first)` saw some of these children who work in the Cotton Mills, trying to play after `text(hours)`. I say “trying to play” because they seemed hardly to have the strength to play. . . . Surely the children’s health is more important than additional luxuries for the stockholders.

	—Suzanne Heber, New York, `1916`

:box:Dear Sir, We most earnestly protest the passage of the [child labor bill]. . . . It would bring hardship on a large number of people, such as widows and infirm parents who are wholly dependent on such labor for a living. . . . We have state laws in South Carolina that give us all the protection we need.

	—Cotton mill owners from South Carolina, `1916`
With which statement would Suzanne Heber most likely agree?

A.Choice: Children should be able to decide what is best for themselves.

B.Choice: The government has a responsibility to protect children in society.

Key.Rationale: Suzanne Heber would most likely agree with the idea that government has a responsibility to protect children in society.

C.Choice: The states have the right to make all the laws about children’s activities.

D.Choice: Business owners are very concerned about the well-being of their child workers.

Read the information and quotation in the boxes.

:box:During the `text(1960s)`, many people in the United States became concerned about problems in the environment. The air and waterways were being polluted, and the use of pesticides was damaging wildlife. Senator Gaylord Nelson of Wisconsin founded Earth Day in `1970` as a way to educate people about environmental issues. People have continued to celebrate Earth Day `text(each year)`, and it has now spread to more than `170` countries.

:box:Our goal is not just an environment of clean air and water and scenic beauty. The objective is an environment of decency, quality, and mutual respect for all other human beings and all other living creatures.

	—Senator Gaylord Nelson, speaking at the `text(first)` Earth Day in `1970`
How have the events of the `text(first)` Earth Day affected life today?

A.Choice: All environmental problems have been solved.

B.Choice: People continue to work to protect the environment.

Key.Rationale: People continue to work to protect the environment.

C.Choice: There is no longer a need for events such as Earth Day.

D.Choice: People in other countries are not interested in the goals of Earth Day.

:box:`ultext(Facts about Dams in Wisconsin)`

• Wisconsin has `text(15,000)` lakes and `text(84,000 miles)` of rivers and streams.
• Wisconsin has `text(3,900)` dams.
• Wisconsin’s first dam was built in `1809` to provide power for a sawmill. `text(Two)` more dams were built in `1819` and `1831` to power lumber and grain mills.
• About `900` dams in Wisconsin have been removed, some for safety and environmental reasons.
What is `text(one)` way dams have helped people in Wisconsin over time?

A.Choice: They have improved the air quality.

C.Choice: They have provided energy for businesses.

Key.Rationale: Dams have helped people in Wisconsin by providing energy for businesses.

D.Choice: They have allowed the state to expand in size.
